3effd841a42c81219f69e3a513b2d557.name: Columnar joints formed by a pyroclastic flow
3effd841a42c81219f69e3a513b2d557.description: Columns formed when a pyroclastic flow from a large eruption about 30,000 years ago welded itself solid with its own heat, then cracked as it cooled and shrank. They formed differently from the columns at Tojinbo or Genbudo, which came from cooling magma or lava.

3effd841a42c8195abc8e9e53b3e86f3.name: A gorge carved by the Ishikari River
3effd841a42c8195abc8e9e53b3e86f3.description: A gorge formed as the Ishikari River cut deeper and deeper into the columnar-jointed rock. At Obako, the river flows between sheer rock walls on both banks.

3effd841a42c81da898bc4b8a16b5583.name: Sobakudai Observatory
3effd841a42c81da898bc4b8a16b5583.description: A viewpoint where you can see Ginga Falls and Ryusei Falls at the same time. From the Taki Mintara building, climb the steep stairs, passing the first viewpoint and a spot with a bench. The visitor center gives the walk as about 25 minutes; the tourism association says about 20.
3effd841a42c81da898bc4b8a16b5583.note: Some sections are narrow, so watch your step. Carry a bell or something else that makes noise, so you don't surprise wild animals.

3effd841a42c81379574c362d7e60830.name: Fudo-iwa Rock
3effd841a42c81379574c362d7e60830.description: A sheer cliff rising between Ginga Falls and Ryusei Falls. The two waterfalls pour down on either side of it.

3effd841a42c814c9ba9f8b4d04f9300.name: The 九十九沢 stream and its “phantom” falls
3effd841a42c814c9ba9f8b4d04f9300.description: A stream that flows down from about 1,800 m on the east slope of Mt. Kurodake. Its underground water has been chosen as one of Hokkaido's famous waters, and it is also used as Sounkyo's everyday water supply. The falls (九十九滝) are a “phantom waterfall” that appears only when the water rises and groundwater pours down the cliff.
3effd841a42c814c9ba9f8b4d04f9300.when: The falls appear only in the snowmelt season (usually around early May) or after heavy rain

3effd841a42c814bb8fce23e07ab09fa.name: Madara-suzu cricket
3effd841a42c814bb8fce23e07ab09fa.description: A tiny cricket, 6–7 mm long. In the lowlands it is a summer insect, but at hot spring areas warmed by geothermal heat it is known to sing even in winter, and in Momijidani it can be seen all year.

3effd841a42c819e9ef9efda8fedb65e.name: Autumn leaves
3effd841a42c819e9ef9efda8fedb65e.description: The area around the trail entrance is the hot spring town's best-known spot for autumn color. Full-moon maple and Japanese rowan turn red to orange, while painted maple, katsura and Erman's birch turn yellow.

3effd841a42c81ff8d3ad753639c97ad.name: Big monarch birch
3effd841a42c81ff8d3ad753639c97ad.description: A member of the birch family that gives the finest timber of them all. Its wood is so much better than that of other birches that it is called makaba, “the true birch”.

3effd841a42c819495b2dc5e9d0c8759.name: Tengu's Millstone Rock (天狗の引き臼岩)
3effd841a42c819495b2dc5e9d0c8759.description: A rock named after words in a song by Noguchi Ujo, the children's-song poet who visited Sounkyo in 1927.

3effd841a42c814c927ae2caaa931935.name: Japanese crayfish stream
3effd841a42c814c927ae2caaa931935.description: A crayfish found only in Japan, living only in Hokkaido and parts of the Tohoku region. It is small, 4–8 cm long, and dark brown. In the Edo period, the stones that form inside its body were prized as medicine.
3effd841a42c814c927ae2caaa931935.note: Please only look at living things — don't catch them.

3effd841a42c81a7a809dc5173a8bdc9.name: Frost-cracked tree
3effd841a42c81a7a809dc5173a8bdc9.description: A tree split lengthwise when the water inside its trunk froze and expanded in midwinter. This happens especially often to Sakhalin fir.
3effd841a42c81a7a809dc5173a8bdc9.when: The cracks can be seen all year (they form in midwinter)

3effd841a42c81269d98f21b1178f4fb.name: Hot spring sources
3effd841a42c81269d98f21b1178f4fb.description: Sounkyo has more than 30 places where hot spring water comes out of the ground, at 46–93°C; the water is a simple spring. More than 20 of them are packed into an area of about 200 m × 100 m around the Momijidani parking lot — the densest cluster in Sounkyo.

3effd841a42c810d8785c4c19ff7abbb.name: Bear tree
3effd841a42c810d8785c4c19ff7abbb.description: A tree that still carries a brown bear's claw marks. A kokuwa (hardy kiwi) vine used to wind around this tree, and the marks are said to be from a bear that climbed up when the fruit was ripe.
3effd841a42c810d8785c4c19ff7abbb.note: Momijidani is brown bear habitat. Carry a bell or something else that makes noise as you walk.

3effd841a42c816a9c8feb30d1562c5b.name: Katsura tree
3effd841a42c816a9c8feb30d1562c5b.description: Said to grow bigger than any other tree in Hokkaido, reaching 20–30 m tall and 1–2 m across. When its leaves turn yellow in autumn, they give off a sweet smell.

3effd841a42c81d49fdae51e15bac079.name: Akaishi River (赤石川)
3effd841a42c81d49fdae51e15bac079.description: Its Ainu name is Shumahurepet (シュマフーレペッ: stone, red, river). About 10 km long, it flows out from the floor of the old crater of Ohachidaira. Upstream, hydrogen sulfide from fumaroles makes it strongly acidic, with recorded pH values of 3.1–3.6.

3effd841a42c81c3beace9f61151a228.name: Black woodpecker feeding tree
3effd841a42c81c3beace9f61151a228.description: A tree marked where a black woodpecker pecked for food. With its black body and red on the back of its head, the black woodpecker is Japan's largest woodpecker and a national natural monument. In Ainu it is called Chiptachikam Kamuy (チプタチカム・カムイ).

3effd841a42c815eba00db0f43c1525c.name: Ezo flying squirrel
3effd841a42c815eba00db0f43c1525c.description: Lives in Hokkaido's forests, from the lowlands up to the subalpine zone. It glides from tree to tree by spreading the membrane between its front and back legs.

3effd841a42c81448ff5fcbf0c391a93.name: Nurse logs
3effd841a42c81448ff5fcbf0c391a93.description: Seeds land on fallen trees and stumps, sprout, and grow into the next generation of trees. It is one of the ways a forest renews itself.

3effd841a42c81068d7bd69e0ecaa519.name: Onko Rock
3effd841a42c81068d7bd69e0ecaa519.description: Named for the Japanese yew (called onko in Hokkaido) that grows draped over this large rock beside the trail. In Ainu the yew is called rarumani (ラルマニ). About a 10-minute walk from the Akaishi River junction.

3effd841a42c8192a62ec025b94d13a6.name: Kolomikta vine
3effd841a42c8192a62ec025b94d13a6.description: A woody vine that grows by climbing other trees and rocks. Around flowering time, its leaves turn pink.
3effd841a42c8192a62ec025b94d13a6.when: The leaves change color at flowering time

3effd841a42c8140934ad3efef601814.name: Columnar joints
3effd841a42c8140934ad3efef601814.description: Cracks that formed as welded tuff cooled and shrank, leaving the rock lined up like columns. In cross-section the columns are hexagons and other polygons. In Momijidani you can see these rock walls right in front of you.

3effd841a42c81a1a8fec4d6401174d0.name: Momiji Falls
3effd841a42c81a1a8fec4d6401174d0.description: A two-tiered waterfall about 10 m high at the end of the trail. It is the farthest-downstream waterfall on the Akaishi River, which flows from the old crater of Ohachidaira. The tourism association writes its name as 紅葉の滝.

3effd841a42c812ca9f1f0a020478f08.name: Flowers of Momijidani
3effd841a42c812ca9f1f0a020478f08.description: More than 150 plant species can be seen around Momijidani. Around mid-May, Anemone debilis and Anemone flaccida bloom first; in late June come Aruncus and Trautvetteria, and from July on, Lilium medeoloides, Ezo monkshood and others follow. Photos of bunchberry, Rhododendron albrechtii, Weigela middendorffiana and more are in the visitor center's flower guide (in Japanese).
3effd841a42c812ca9f1f0a020478f08.note: Please only look at plants — don't pick them.

3effd841a42c8133a08cfecefc6cf951.name: Ezo red fox and Ezo sika deer
3effd841a42c8133a08cfecefc6cf951.description: On the trail you may sometimes meet an Ezo red fox, or a sika deer mother with her fawn (from the visitor center's record photos).
3effd841a42c8133a08cfecefc6cf951.note: Please don't approach or feed wild animals.

3effd841a42c8184bc2afb811e5a0545.name: Frost flowers
3effd841a42c8184bc2afb811e5a0545.description: Frost crystals that grow into flower-like shapes, recorded in Momijidani in winter.

3effd841a42c81b384a4c335d42d5401.name: Spray icicles
3effd841a42c81b384a4c335d42d5401.description: Ice shapes that form in winter when spray from the water freezes. The visitor center has recorded them in Momijidani in winter.

3effd841a42c8128a173d7009ee23813.name: Snowshoe walks in winter
3effd841a42c8128a173d7009ee23813.description: In winter the whole trail is covered in snow, so you walk on snowshoes. The route gets hard to follow, so walking with a guide or joining a nature walk event is recommended.
3effd841a42c8128a173d7009ee23813.note: Do not go in when the weather is bad, the path is icy, or there is a risk of avalanches.

3d0fd841a42c812083ddc3ffb0c4b2bd.name: Momijidani
3d0fd841a42c812083ddc3ffb0c4b2bd.season: June to early November (tourism association). In winter you can walk it on snowshoes (visitor center; going with a guide or joining a nature walk is recommended)
3d0fd841a42c812083ddc3ffb0c4b2bd.access: About 15 minutes on foot from the hot spring town to the entrance. From the entrance to Momiji Falls: about 700 m, about 30 minutes one way

3edfd841a42c812098ebf738e7df8d7a.name: Momiji Falls
3edfd841a42c812098ebf738e7df8d7a.season: June to early November. Reachable on snowshoes in winter
3edfd841a42c812098ebf738e7df8d7a.access: At the end of the Momijidani trail. About 700 m, about 30 minutes one way from the entrance

3d0fd841a42c819eab89eb0ebb6ba18b.name: Ginga Falls & Ryusei Falls
3d0fd841a42c819eab89eb0ebb6ba18b.access: You can see them up close from the parking lot. About 20 minutes up the slope to Sobakudai Observatory

3d0fd841a42c812ca17ad8a184d866ce.name: Obako
3d0fd841a42c812ca17ad8a184d866ce.access: About 6 km from the hot spring town toward Kitami; on the left just past the new Obako tunnel
